subject: microbiology
title: Hypersensitivity I: Type I, Anaphylaxis, Arthus Reaction and Serum Sickness

steps.tx: **Type I hypersensitivity** is IgE mediated immediate allergy: first exposure sensitises (allergen specific IgE arms mast cells and basophils via Fc epsilon receptors), re exposure crosslinks that IgE within minutes, releasing histamine, tryptase, prostaglandins and leukotrienes into wheal and flare, rhinitis, asthma or anaphylaxis. Early phase minutes, late phase hours with eosinophils recruited behind.
steps.say: Sensitise silently, trigger in minutes: crosslinked IgE is allergy's loaded spring.

nodes.label: First exposure: allergen specific IgE made
IgE arms mast cells for weeks
Histamine and lipid mediators released in minutes

steps.tx: **Anaphylaxis** is type I at systemic scale: airway oedema and bronchospasm, vasodilation and capillary leak collapsing pressure, urticaria often but not always, treated immediately with intramuscular adrenaline (thigh, repeat every five minutes) before antihistamines or steroids, which are adjuncts only. Serum tryptase later confirms mast cell degranulation for the allergy workup.
steps.say: Adrenaline intramuscularly first and fast; everything else in anaphylaxis is supporting cast.

left.title: Anaphylaxis portrait
points: Triggers: foods, drugs, venom, latex, contrast traditions
Skin signs absent in a minority, shock leads

right.title: Anaphylaxis answers
points: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg adult thigh, repeat 5 minutely
Lie flat, legs raised, oxygen and fluids
Auto injector training and allergy referral after

steps.tx: **Type II hypersensitivity** is antibody against cell surface antigen: IgG and IgM fix complement and recruit phagocytes and NK cells onto blood cells (transfusion reactions, haemolytic disease of newborn, autoimmune cytopenias), drug haptens on membranes, and receptor antibodies stimulating (Graves) or blocking (myasthenia) as its functional fifth column.
steps.say: Antibody stuck on a cell surface marks that cell for complement, phagocytes or dysfunction.

left.title: Cytotoxic type II
points: Haemolytic disease of the newborn (anti D)
Autoimmune haemolytic anaemia and ITP mechanisms
Drug induced cytopenias (hapten and immune complex routes)

right.title: Receptor type II variants
points: Myasthenia: acetylcholine receptor blockade and loss

steps.tx: **Type III hypersensitivity** is immune complex disease: soluble complexes deposit in vessels, glomeruli and joints, fix complement and summon neutrophils whose enzymes injure the wall (vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis). Serum sickness and Arthus are its experimental twins below; lupus and post infectious glomerulonephritis its clinical heirs.
steps.say: Complexes deposit, complement burns, neutrophils injure: small vessel vasculitis by recipe.

left.title: Type III mechanics
points: Antigen antibody complexes in slight antigen excess deposit
Neutrophil lysosomal injury and fibrinoid necrosis

steps.tx: The **Arthus reaction** is localised type III: a sensitised animal (or patient after repeated insulin or vaccines historically) injected intradermally develops haemorrhagic necrotic oedema in 4 to 10 hours as complexes form in vessel walls at the site. It taught that antibody excess locally can be as destructive as any toxin.
steps.say: Hours, local, haemorrhagic: Arthus is serum sickness in one square of skin.

left.title: Arthus portrait
points: Onset 4 to 10 hours, oedema and haemorrhage
Resolves over days, necrosis may ulcerate

right.title: Clinical echoes
points: Farmer lung has type III components (with IV)
Distinguished from delayed type IV by hours and antibody

steps.tx: **Serum sickness** is systemic type III after foreign protein (historical antitoxins, modern monoclonals, antithymocyte globulin, some antibiotics): 7 to 14 days after first exposure (faster on re exposure) fever, rash, arthralgia, lymphadenopathy and low complement declare circulating complexes, resolving as antigen clears, treated supportively and with steroids when severe; drug fever mimics line its differential.
steps.say: Seven to fourteen days after foreign protein, complexes announce themselves in joints, skin and complement.

left.title: Serum sickness portrait
points: Fever, urticarial and morbilliform rash, arthralgia

right.title: Modern causes
points: Beta lactams and other drug serum sickness like reactions

steps.tx: **Gell and Coombs classification** itself needs placing: types I to III antibody mediated (minutes to hours to days), type IV T cell mediated (days), with modern additions (receptor functional antibodies) filed under II. Examination stems give the disease and ask the type, so disease to mechanism pairing is the skill, not list recitation.
steps.say: Pair every disease to its mechanism hour by hour: minutes I, hours II and III, days IV.

left.title: Antibody types
points: II variants: receptor stimulation and blockade

right.title: Cellular type
points: IV: T cells and macrophages, 48 to 72 hours
Subtypes IVa to IVd by cytokine and effector

steps.tx: **Allergy testing hierarchy** applies type I: history first (timing, trigger, reproducibility), skin prick and specific IgE confirming sensitisation (not clinical allergy alone), component resolved diagnostics refining nut and venom risk, and supervised challenge as gold standard where history and tests disagree. Tryptase, total IgE and eosinophils support, never replace, the story.
steps.say: Sensitisation is a test result; allergy is a history the test must match.

left.title: Testing tools
points: Skin prick: wheal versus controls in 15 minutes
Specific IgE: blood alternative when skin impossible
Component diagnostics: Ara h2 peanut risk class

right.title: Testing traps
points: Positive test without history: sensitisation only
Food panels without history mislead elimination diets
